note: Orders every 2 days (even days) for 1.1× forecast over the two days covered, which balances the 54 fixed cost against holding cost; the risk is that a random-walk shortage builds up when demand runs high.
Daily orders at 1.1× forecast keep holding cost minimal; the risk is that 25×54 in fixed costs eats the gain.
Orders every 3 days, trimmed to fit the warehouse; the risk is overflow against the 152 limit, losing paid goods, plus higher holding cost.
Every 2 days at exactly the forecast, so minimal holding; the risk is shortages and penalties because mean demand runs ~4.6% above forecast.
Every 2 days with a large 1.25× safety margin to almost eliminate penalties; the risk is surplus building up, raising holding cost and capacity overflow around day 9.
Every 2 days at 1.15×, a middle ground between penalties and holding; the risk is accumulated surplus and paying for storage on it.
Every 2 days on odd days (day 0 covers only day 5), 1.1×, with the final delivery covering days 28–29; the risk is the extra order on day 0 and the same random walk of shortages.
Every 2 days: build safety stock early (1.2×), then 1.05× in the middle and 0.95× at the end so stock isn't left over; the risk is an end-of-horizon shortage when demand spikes.
